title: TATB 3
speaker: Zoketsu Norman Fischer
summary: Zoketsu Norman Fischer takes up verses 6 through 15 of the text under study, which continue the discussion of the eighth consciousness, the alaya vijnana. Before getting into the technicalities, Norman backs up to ask why a Buddhist account of consciousness is worth studying at all. Norman describes these teachings as dialectical antidotes to the mistaken ideas of reality that everyone carries, since "everybody is a philosopher," whether or not a book was ever read. The test of those ideas is suffering, and the Buddhist remedy is to set an opposing idea against them until nothing remains but zero, neutrality, and the freedom to live. The passage closes on the claim that what a person is and what consciousness is differ from what we think.
